cells.tense: You are here, pen in hand, at the end of something that finished well.
cells.verb: Watching what you imagined come true and feeling the full weight of its arrival
cells.place: Standing in the doorway where completion turns into departure
cells.ask: Offer the momentum forward — let this finish feed the next thing, not because it's owed, but because it's ready to. What comes back is direction that arises from genuine engagement: you'll move not from pressure but from feeling.
cells.core: You're the one who knows what it feels like when a vision finally lands — not perfect, but deeply felt, fully lived. The satisfaction isn't loud; it's in the bones. What you carry is the quiet authority of someone who stayed with the imagining until it became real. That arrival is yours to claim.
cells.sheetLine: You imagined it, you felt it, and it's here.

cells.tense: You are bracing for a future you can't write in yet, already rehearsing the satisfaction that hasn't arrived.
cells.verb: Chasing the feeling of completion before it's actually here, forcing the ending ahead of its time
cells.place: Standing at a finish line you've drawn in your own head, running toward it before the race has been run
cells.ask: Tend one thing that's actually growing — give it care without forcing its pace. When this balance returns, growth happens without exhausting you; you hold space without clutching. Let what's alive move at its own speed.
cells.core: You're projecting yourself into the satisfaction before it's earned, and the pushing is hollowing out the present. The vision is real, but you're trying to skip the integration — demanding the feeling of arrival before you've actually arrived. What you want can't be manufactured ahead of time; it has to be lived into.
cells.sheetLine: You're demanding the harvest while the field is still growing.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you, looking back instead of turning the knob.
cells.verb: Holding the feeling of what was finished without letting it become a departure
cells.place: Stuck in the threshold of completion, unable to step through into what's next
cells.ask: Sit with what you already know — let it settle without needing to act on it yet. When this balance returns, your vision flows from genuine integration: you dream because experience has been fully processed. Direct knowing lands without argument.
cells.core: You've been at the end of something for a while now, but you haven't let it finish. The satisfaction that should have carried you forward has become a place you keep circling. What's missing isn't more dreaming — it's the quiet, inner knowing that it's done, and that done is allowed to become departure.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the completion but you won't let it release you.

cells.tense: You are already writing the next chapter while telling yourself you're just waiting for the ink to dry.
cells.verb: Living from an integrated vision while calling it something that happened to you
cells.place: Standing in a room you've already left, telling the story as if you're still in it
cells.ask: Refine one thing with careful attention — practice without forcing it to mean more than it does. When this balance returns, solitude connects rather than isolates, and refinement serves growth rather than worry. Distinguish what matters from what doesn't.
cells.core: You've already integrated what you imagined — it's shaping how you move and what you choose — but you keep describing it as if it were still happening to you. The steering is already yours; the saying-so isn't. You're at the wheel without admitting it, and the truest thing you could do is say you've been driving.
cells.sheetLine: You're already moving from it. You just haven't called it yours.
